findings.title: Team permission check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This only allows users who are both team admin and team owner; team admins who are not owners are denied. The intended check appears to be admin OR owner, so the endpoint's authorization does not match the variable name and likely product intent.

findings.title: Guest emails are not deduplicated or normalized before insert
findings.body: The handler filters guests only against already-persisted attendees. It does not deduplicate the incoming guests array or normalize email casing. A request containing the same email twice, or case variants of an existing attendee email, can pass the filter and create duplicate attendee records and duplicate email sends. Server-side validation should dedupe and normalize emails rather than relying on the dialog.

findings.title: Blacklist check can be bypassed by casing or whitespace
findings.body: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, but the incoming guest email is not lowercased or trimmed before the includes check. A blacklisted address submitted as `Foo@Example.com` or with surrounding whitespace can bypass the blacklist.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the original guests list instead of the filtered list
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original input array after the handler has computed uniqueGuests. If the request included an existing attendee email, that attendee is treated as a new guest for email selection and can receive the wrong email; duplicates in the input can also cause duplicate emails. Pass the filtered/deduped new guest list instead.

findings.title: Any attendee can modify the guest list
findings.body: The permission check treats any attendee whose email matches the authenticated user's email as allowed to add guests. This lets a participant, not just the organizer/host, modify the guest list and trigger invitation emails to arbitrary addresses. Unless this is an explicit product decision, the endpoint should restrict this action to hosts/team admins.

findings.title: Endpoint does not validate booking status
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking but never checks its status or timing. The API can therefore add guests to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings even if the UI hides the action. This can send notifications and update calendar events for bookings that should no longer be modified.

findings.title: No limit on number of guest emails
findings.body: guests is validated only as an array of email strings with no maximum length. An authenticated user can submit a very large array, causing a large createMany operation and mass email sending. Add a reasonable max length.

findings.title: Organizer lookup can throw for bookings without a user
findings.body: The organizer lookup uses `booking.userId || 0` with findFirstOrThrow. If a booking has no userId, for example in some team/round-robin cases, this queries user id 0 and throws a Prisma not-found error, producing a 500 instead of handling the missing organizer.

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before calendar update without a transaction
findings.body: Attendees are persisted with prisma.booking.update before calling eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and the whole operation is not transactional. If the calendar update fails, guests remain attached to the booking while the client receives an error, leaving Cal.com attendees and external calendar attendees inconsistent.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore email-disable settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails does not accept or check event-type email disable settings, unlike other email-sending helpers. Add-guests notifications will be sent even when standard host/attendee emails are disabled for the event type.

findings.title: Invalid-email error state is not reset after successful submission
findings.body: The mutation success handler closes the dialog and resets the email list but does not reset isInvalidEmail. If a previous submission failed validation and a later submission succeeds, reopening the dialog can still show the stale validation error.

findings.title: Error toast fallback is never used
findings.body: The error message is built with a template string that is always non-empty, so the fallback to t('unable_to_add_guests') never runs. Users may see a message like `undefined: ...` when no TRPC error code is present.

findings.title: To address can be malformed for guests with empty name
findings.body: New guest attendees are created with an empty name, and the email sets `to` to `${attendee.name} <${attendee.email}>`. This can produce a malformed display name such as ` <guest@example.com>`. Use the email address as a fallback when name is empty.

findings.title: Hard-coded English tooltip
findings.body: The remove-email tooltip content is hard-coded as 'Remove email' instead of using the translation hook, so it will not be localized.

findings.title: No tests for the new add-guests endpoint
findings.body: No automated tests are added for the new tRPC endpoint, including its permission logic, duplicate/blacklisted email handling, and email selection. These are security-sensitive paths that would benefit from regression tests.
